Understanding Curves with a Compass

A curve drawn on paper using only a pencil and compass is called a circle. To draw a circle, fix the point of the compass at a specific location (the center) and move the pencil along the edge while keeping the distance constant. The shape formed is always a circle.

Circle Properties

In a circle, every point on the curve is equidistant from the center point. This distance is called the radius. If you measure the distance from the center to any point on the circle, it will always be equal to the radius.

Understanding Curves with a Compass

A curve drawn on paper using only a pencil and compass is called a circle. To draw a circle, fix the point of the compass at a specific location (the center) and move the pencil along the edge while keeping the distance constant. The shape formed is always a circle.

Circle Properties

In a circle, every point on the curve is equidistant from the center point. This distance is called the radius. If you measure the distance from the center to any point on the circle, it will always be equal to the radius.
